jobs.title: Director, AI Operations
jobs.description:
Overview

Microsoft's Corporate, External & Legal Affairs (CELA) organization supports one of the most complex commercial operations in the world. The Customer & Partner Solutions (CPS) group is where legal meets the commercial engine, supporting the Microsoft Commercial Business, Microsoft Elevate, the Deal Desk, and thousands of customer and partner interactions every year.

The Director, AI Operations sits at the center of that intersection. You will own the operational and technology strategy that enables CELA CPS to function as a modern, AI-powered legal organization, developing the platforms our teams depend on daily and driving AI adoption at scale. You will also lead the small technology team that delivers this work, and will lead the virtual teams that carry connected-service development across CPS.

This is not a policy role or a staff function. This is a delivery role in which you will be expected to move programs from concept to production, build trusted relationships across legal and engineering, and operate effectively across organizational layers.

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more, and we're dedicated to this mission across every aspect of our company. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. Join us and help shape the future of the world.

Responsibilities

Team Leadership

You are the manager of the CPS technology team and the owner of its operating model. That means setting the direction, holding the leadership team to a shared definition of success, and making sure the work is treated as a team sport rather than a set of individual projects.

Set the vision, definition of success, metrics, and benchmarking for CPS technology work, and establish leadership team alignment behind that model.
Manage, coach, and set priorities for the CPS Legal Engineer and the CPS Content Lead, including talent assessment and role remapping as the model matures.
Lead the virtual teams that carry connected-service delivery, drawing resources from across CPS and the wider CELA organization.
Own intake and tradeoff decisions across competing technology requests, including the weekly prioritization rhythm with the leadership team.

CPS Connected Systems

Own and drive the FY27+ platform strategy that expands upon our existing Microsoft Dynamics CRM and matter management platform. This includes partnering with engineering counterparts to translate legal-operations requirements into delivered product, and then rolling it out to hundreds of legal professionals worldwide.

CELA Frontline Operations

Oversee and expand the technology infrastructure that supports CELA's first-response legal support function serving over 100,000 Microsoft Commercial Business and Microsoft Elevate clients. This includes further innovating the platform and implementing process improvements based on data and user experience.

AI Adoption and Third-Party Solutions

Lead the rollout and ongoing expansion of existing first- and third-party AI tools and solutions across CPS. This includes working closely with internal engineering teams and vendors, our legal professionals and our internal clients to drive deep technical integration and cultural adoption of these key solutions.

Executive Engagement and Transparency

You will often function as the face of CPS technology work with internal and external executives. This includes leading regular internal business reviews, meeting with technology partners on build/buy assessments, and explaining our work with other legal technology teams worldwide.

Culture

Embody our culture and values.
Foster inclusive practices and ensure diverse perspectives are heard.
Support colleagues and clients with empathy and respect.
Embrace a global mindset, respecting similarities and differences in others.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in relevant field (e.g., Liberal Arts, Business Administration, Management, Computer Science) AND 8+ years experience in financial management, business planning, operations management, strategy, project management, human resources or business-related roles OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's Degree in relevant field (e.g., Liberal Arts, Business Administration, Management, Computer Science) AND 12+ years experience in financial management, business planning, operations management, strategy, project management, human resources, or business-related roles OR Bachelor's Degree in relevant field (e.g., Liberal Arts, Business Administration, Management, Computer Science) AND 15+ years experience in financial management, business planning, operations management, strategy, project management, human resources, or business-related roles OR equivalent experience.
5+ years people management experience.
10+ years of progressive experience in legal operations, legal technology, or a closely adjacent field, such as enterprise program delivery in a regulated industry.
Demonstrated ability to own and ship technology programs end to end.
Experience managing or leading a small team, including setting priorities, coaching, and assessing talent against a changing operating model.
Experience operating in a large, matrixed global organization with multiple executive stakeholders.
Ability to translate between legal, engineering, and commercial audiences without losing meaning in either direction.
Comfort with ambiguity, as this role spans strategy and execution and you need to be effective at both.
Familiarity with Microsoft's commercial and legal infrastructure (MCAPS, CPS, CELA).
Hands-on experience with AI legal tools such as Harvey or Copilot, and a genuine interest in driving AI adoption at scale.
Experience managing vendor partnerships, including SSPA and security compliance reviews and license governance.
Fluency in legal operations concepts: matter management, outside-counsel governance, paralegal-support models, and client intake.
Prior work in content governance, communications strategy, or knowledge management.

Job Summary:

We are seeking an experienced Power Generation Operations Director to lead and oversee both primary and secondary generation systems at our U.S. data center sites. This role will be responsible for the development and execution of methods and procedures (MOPs) to ensure the continuous protection of compute load—particularly during load transfers and ramp rate transitions. The Director will partner closely with operations training teams to build, implement, and continually improve repair and maintenance programs. Additional responsibilities include managing power plant agreements for on-site power generation and directly recruiting and managing teams to operate power equipment, with a focus on achieving 100% equipment availability.

Key Responsibilities:

Lead, supervise, and develop teams responsible for the operations and maintenance of both primary and secondary power generation assets.
Develop, document, and maintain comprehensive MOPs to guarantee compute load protection during generation transitions, including detailed ramp rate controls.
Collaborate with operations training teams to create and deliver effective repair and maintenance training programs for all generation system staff.
Oversee the negotiation, execution, and ongoing management of power plant agreements for on-site generation, ensuring alignment with operational requirements and uptime targets.
Directly recruit, hire, and lead specialized teams as needed to operate on-site power generation equipment, maintaining 100% system availability.
Establish, monitor, and report on performance metrics related to power system reliability, efficiency, and responsiveness to critical incidents.
Champion a culture of safety, compliance, and continuous improvement, ensuring adherence to all regulatory requirements and corporate standards.
Serve as the primary escalation point for high-severity power incidents, coordinating rapid and effective resolution.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of industry best practices, emerging technologies, and regulatory changes affecting power system operations.

10+ years of experience in power generation operations, with 5+ years in a leadership or director-level capacity.
Deep knowledge of primary and secondary on-site power generation technologies and their integration into mission-critical facilities.
Proven expertise in developing MOPs to manage compute load protection and ramp rate adherence.
Strong background in building effective training, repair, and preventive maintenance programs.

Exceptional leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Experience with regulatory compliance (e.g., NERC, FERC, OSHA, EPA) for power operations.

Data Center Site Portfolio Management:

Data Center country leader and typically has responsibility for one or more sites & teams in a region.

Defines strategic direction for network performance evaluation, collaborates with executive leadership.

jobs.description:
GROW YOUR CAREER WITH US

At Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings (NCLH), we know our future success depends on our ability to attract and retain the very best talent. Our brands deliver vacations of a lifetime with innovative product offerings, a high level of service and unique guest experiences aboard each vessel and we’re continually seeking applicants who are passionate about hospitality and committed to being their personal best. Job Summary

The Senior Director, Mobile Applications is responsible for enterprise-wide execution and operational excellence of all branded mobile applications across the full guest journey. This role leads Research, Design, Experimentation, Product Management, and Front-End Technology for mobile platforms supporting acquisition, pre-cruise, onboard, post-cruise, and offline experiences. The Senior Director is accountable for translating stakeholder-defined product priorities into high-quality, scalable, and reliable mobile solutions through disciplined execution of the software development lifecycle (SDLC). The Senior Director oversees budgets, planning, stakeholder alignment, and delivery of projects, enhancements, and maintenance initiatives while managing a hybrid model of internal teams and managed service provider (MSP) partners. This role ensures innovation, scalability, and measurable business value while driving AI adoption and future AI product integration within the mobile ecosystem. Partner with stakeholders to translate mobile product strategies and priorities into executable delivery roadmaps.
Provide input to inform feasibility, sequencing, capacity planning, and dependency management.
Lead multidisciplinary teams spanning Product Management, UX/UI Design, Research, Front-End Engineering, Release Management, and Experimentation functions.
Oversee delivery of all mobile initiatives including large-scale projects, feature enhancements, experimentation programs, and production maintenance.

Champion innovation, collaboration, transparency, and passion across mobile and cross-functional teams.

Build and mentor a specialized team of network architects focused on high-performance GPU infrastructure.

12+ overall years of proven experience in networking, cloud infrastructure, or distributed systems with 5+ years of experience directly managing technical teams.
Mastery of data center networking, including Clos/spine-leaf architectures and high-performance fabrics like RDMA, RoCE, or InfiniBand.
Hands-on experience with BGP, EVPN/VXLAN, and kernel-level development for routing and switching.
Skilled in using Ansible or Terraform for infrastructure automation, paired with monitoring tools like Prometheus and Grafana.
Practical experience designing for large-scale configurations using SR-IOV, Xen virtualization, or Open Virtual Switch.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related engineering field (or equivalent experience).
Ability to ensure all infrastructure meets rigorous internal policies and regulatory standards like GDPR.

Proven success managing networking for large-scale GPU clusters or hyperscale cloud environments.
Familiarity with optical networking and high-speed interconnects reaching 400G or 800G.
Experience in debugging and improving code for Mellanox/Cumulus Linux or managing Palo Alto and Netscaler appliances.
A strong grasp of streaming telemetry and operational signals (SNMP, Syslog) to proactively resolve complex architectural bottlenecks.
Relevant top-tier certifications, such as CCIE or specialized cloud networking designations.

You'll be responsible for designing and commissioning white space deployments — taking pre-built environments and fitting them out with the power distribution, cooling distribution, and systems infrastructure needed to run high-density GPU workloads at scale. At the same time, you'll be building the break-fix and smart hands team from scratch: hiring, defining the playbook, and standing up the function that keeps our sites running around the clock.

This is not a steady-state operations role. It's a builder role. You'll be joining a small but fast-moving team, with real ownership over outcomes and the autonomy to shape how Together AI operates its physical infrastructure for years to come. If you've scaled data center infrastructure through hypergrowth before and want to do it again with more ownership — this is that opportunity.

Build and lead a ~20-person break-fix and smart hands team from scratch — define the operating model, hire the initial team, and establish the processes and playbooks that keep sites running
Manage a portfolio of 5+ sites across two regions in various stages of deployment and live operation
Partner with vendors, contractors, and equipment suppliers to drive site deployments to schedule and quality
Establish operational standards, runbooks, and escalation processes for a nascent but rapidly growing infrastructure function
Serve as the technical authority on data center infrastructure decisions — from white space evaluation through to live production operation
Travel to Asia periodically to oversee regional site deployments and support the local team

Deep, hands-on technical knowledge of data center power and cooling systems at the IT-adjacent layer — PDUs, CDUs, power distribution, and white space fit-out
Proven experience designing and commissioning data center infrastructure, from evaluation through to live operation
Experience operating data center infrastructure at meaningful scale, supporting large production workloads
People leadership experience — you've hired, developed, and led technical operations teams

The OCI AI Infrastructure Network Operations team operates and improves the RDMA/RoCE and InfiniBand network fabrics that power OCI’s largest AI, GPU, and HPC workloads. Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

About The Role

Jobs Platform is Roblox's multi-tier orchestration system for microservices, powering AI Inference across Roblox. Through a simple developer API, we deliver a "deploy and forget" runtime, hiding the complexity of scheduling, scaling, and reliably running services across our on-prem and multi-cloud footprint at global scale. As Principal Product Manager, Jobs Platform, you'll take the helm at a defining moment - leading the charge as we scale the platform to become the default runtime for critical Roblox services worldwide.

You Will

Own Jobs Platform end-to-end - set the multi-year vision for how Roblox engineers deploy, run, and scale AI and other services across our Core and Edge Datacenters, and cloud.
Power Roblox's AI future - build the platform that brings frontier models and next-gen AI workloads to life, with the primitives, scheduling guarantees, and resource classes AI teams need to move fast.
Evolve the platform's technical core - define how Roblox prioritizes, isolates, and preempts workloads across shared fleet, and shape the entire system across global control plane, multi-region orchestration, distributed systems primitives, capacity/state management, DR/failover, and operator-based Kubernetes extensions.
Make developer experience the reason teams choose Jobs Platform - by delivering integrated tooling (CI/CD, telemetry, profiling, tracing) and managing robust SLOs via real-time fleet signals (health, queue depth, scheduling efficiency)—all while engineering a frictionless, effortless onboarding experience for teams.
Architect intelligent, predictive scaling - advance Multi-Cloud Bursting from reactive to proactive with AI-powered prediction, and partner with Data Science and Finance on demand forecasting, cost-to-serve analytics, and AI-driven resource optimization.
Own the trade-off calls across efficiency, latency, cost-to-serve and time-to-ship, while maintaining reliability.
Lead cross-functionally, acting as the connective tissue between Jobs Platform Users, and Jobs Platform, AI, and infrastructure engineers.

You Have

7+ years of product management experience building resource orchestration, workload management platforms or large-scale distributed systems
Track record of building developer-facing platforms that engineers genuinely love to use. You have a deep understanding of modern software development lifecycle and developer tooling with a history of abstracting complex infrastructure into clean, maintainable platform schemas.
Built and operated Kubernetes and enterprise-grade service mesh at scale, and you understand the developer pain points around control plane mechanics like etcd scaling and API server bottlenecks. You've shipped custom Operators, Controllers, and CRDs, going beyond vanilla Kubernetes.

Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

The Role

At Hadrian, data is part of the factory's operating system. The scheduler deciding what runs next, models predicting cycle time and demand, systems interpreting engineering drawings, analytics tracking production, and operators understanding what is happening on the floor all depend on the same thing: a trustworthy path from the physical and software systems that generate data to the teams and products that use it.

The Data Platform team owns that path. We build the shared infrastructure for ingestion and CDC, event streaming, the warehouse and lakehouse, orchestration, data contracts, quality, lineage, and the foundational data models that sit underneath Analytics, Data Science, Operations Research, ML, and operational software. Today that includes Snowflake, Iceberg on S3, PeerDB, Redpanda/Kafka, Dagster, dbt, Kubernetes, and protobuf/gRPC. Some of our data begins in conventional software systems. Some begins on CNC machines, inspection equipment, PLCs, engineering files, and the factory floor.

As an Senior Engineering Manager, you will build and lead the team responsible for making this platform reliable, coherent, and useful as Hadrian scales to many factories. You will own the people, execution, operating quality, and direction of the team while staying technically close enough to challenge architecture, understand failure modes, and help engineers make good tradeoffs.

What You’ll Do

Build the team and platform that become Hadrian's data backbone. Lead the engineers responsible for the path from machines and operational systems to the trusted datasets, streams, and interfaces that scheduling, analytics, ML, software, and factory operations depend on.
Own the Data Platform roadmap and delivery. Turn ambiguous needs across Software, Infrastructure, Analytics, Data Science, Operations Research, ML, and Manufacturing into clear priorities, interfaces, owners, and commitments.
Raise the operational bar for the platform: reliability, data-quality SLAs, observability, incident response, backfills and recovery, cost, security, schema evolution, provenance, and clear ownership when something fails.
Partner with senior engineers and technical leads on architecture across CDC and streaming, Snowflake and Iceberg, orchestration, data contracts, schema governance, and the interfaces between the data platform and its consumers. You do not need to design every system yourself, but you need the depth to ask the hard questions and recognize when important semantics or failure modes are missing.
Turn repeated one-off work into paved roads. Build standards, contracts, tooling, documentation, and migration paths that let other engineering and data teams move faster without creating a collection of bespoke pipelines.
Hire and grow an exceptional team. Set a clear technical and performance bar, give direct feedback, develop engineers into broader technical leaders, delegate real ownership, and build a team whose capability grows faster than its headcount.

What We’re Looking For

A track record leading engineers responsible for production data infrastructure, distributed systems, developer platforms, infrastructure, or similarly critical technical systems. For Senior EM, you have led multiple substantial workstreams or teams and developed senior technical leaders.
Strong technical judgment in modern data and platform systems: event streaming and CDC, warehouses and lakehouses, orchestration, schema evolution, data modeling, distributed-system failure modes, and the tradeoffs behind reliable data delivery.
Experience building for environments with real constraints. You understand that the architecture changes when data comes from hardware, machines, devices, files, telemetry, regulated systems, edge environments, or other sources that do not behave like a clean application database.
A real platform mindset. You think in shared abstractions, contracts, ownership, operating guarantees, adoption, migration, deprecation, and paved roads — not just a set of infrastructure components owned by one team.
An operator's mindset. You know what your systems promise, how you know they are healthy, what happens when those promises fail, and how an incident becomes a permanent improvement rather than a recurring story.
Strong people leadership and high agency across organizational boundaries. Your engineers know what is expected of them, where they stand, and how they can grow; when a dependency is blocking the team, you go resolve it rather than simply reporting it upward.

What Will Set You Apart

5+ years of management experience in manufacturing, semiconductors, hardware, robotics, autonomy, industrial systems, test/measurement, or edge computing, especially where the data platform had to bridge software with physical systems. Backgrounds from companies such as NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Xilinx, Altera, Qualcomm, Applied Materials, Lam Research, Tesla, Anduril, Shield AI, or similar environments are especially relevant.
Experience with heterogeneous data beyond application tables: telemetry, events, files, device identity, timestamps and clock drift, units, provenance, schema drift, deletes, late or out-of-order data, partial records, retries, and backfills.
Experience taking a data or infrastructure platform from an early working system to a broadly adopted internal product used by many teams.
Experience operating in security-sensitive or regulated environments such as aerospace, defense, FedRAMP, CMMC, or other environments where data governance and access control are part of the architecture.
A track record of building strong hiring and onboarding systems and helping senior engineers become effective technical leads, Staff+ engineers, or future managers.

Compensation

For this role, the target salary range is $249,000 -
$299,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

Who We Are

Inversion builds advanced reentry systems to deliver next-generation capabilities from space.

Our mission is to make Earth radically more accessible by turning Low-Earth Orbit into an on-demand logistics domain. We see space not as a destination, but as a platform — one that unlocks unprecedented speed and global reach.

Our spacecraft are designed to deliver payloads anywhere on Earth in under an hour, operating through extreme reentry conditions and landing with high precision. These systems open the door to new ways of testing, delivering, and operating at hypersonic speeds.

Inherently dual-use, our technology is built to meet urgent national security needs while laying the groundwork for future commercial applications. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

Snowflake is expanding the boundaries of the Data Cloud to support mission-critical transactional workloads. Our goal is to deliver OLTP capabilities with the performance, reliability, simplicity, and scale customers expect from Snowflake, while creating a seamless experience across transactional and analytical data.

We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager – OLTP
to lead engineering teams and leaders building core transactional database technology and the cloud infrastructure required to operate it at scale. You will help define the architecture and roadmap, grow the organization, and drive technology from design through production.

AS A SENIOR ENGINEERING MANAGER – OLTP AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:

Set technical and execution strategy for key areas of Snowflake's OLTP platform, translating product goals into architecture, roadmaps, and team plans.
Lead and grow multiple engineering teams, developing managers and senior technical leaders while fostering a culture of ownership, technical excellence, and execution.
Drive adoption of AI and agentic development practices to improve engineering velocity, quality, and productivity across the software development lifecycle.
Drive architecture and technical decisions in areas such as transactions, concurrency control, low-latency query processing, storage, indexing, compaction, recovery, replication, and scalability.
Ensure operational readiness and reliability of mission-critical database services, meeting customer commitments for durability, availability, performance, and security through automation, observability, and operational safety.
Drive trade-offs across consistency, latency, throughput, availability, scalability, durability, security, and cost.
Lead major initiatives from design through implementation, launch, and production operation.
Partner with Engineering, Product, and cross-functional leaders to define priorities, align roadmaps, plan staffing, and coordinate execution across organizational boundaries.
Recruit exceptional engineers and engineering leaders, and develop existing team members into larger technical and leadership roles.

OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:

10+ years experience in database internals, OLTP databases, or distributed storage systems.
8+ years leading engineering teams, including multiple teams and managers.
Deep experience with transactions, concurrency, consistency, replication, recovery, storage, and database performance.
Strong understanding of AI-assisted and agentic software development and its application across the engineering lifecycle.
Experience operating mission-critical systems with high standards for availability, durability, observability, operational safety, and incident response.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to drive alignment and influence across organizational boundaries.
Strong hands-on technical ability, including navigating complex codebases and diving deep into system design and implementation.
Experience with OLTP database internals or Postgres internals.
Significant cloud experience across AWS, Azure, and/or GCP, including highly available services.
BS/MS in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience.

WHY JOIN THE OLTP ENGINEERING TEAM AT SNOWFLAKE?

This is an opportunity to help define the next generation of Snowflake's OLTP database platform and expand the workloads customers can bring to the Data Cloud.

You will work on some of the hardest problems in database systems - transactions, concurrency, latency, storage, distributed systems, reliability, and cloud-scale operations - while building and developing the engineering organization needed to solve them.

You will work alongside industry veterans and emerging leaders to create database technology that combines the simplicity and operational experience Snowflake customers expect with the performance and reliability required by mission-critical transactional applications.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

Turning Space into a Transportation Layer for Earth

Who We Are

Inversion builds advanced reentry systems to deliver next-generation capabilities from space.

Our mission is to make Earth radically more accessible by turning Low-Earth Orbit into an on-demand logistics domain. We see space not as a destination, but as a platform — one that unlocks unprecedented speed and global reach.

Our spacecraft are designed to deliver payloads anywhere on Earth in under an hour, operating through extreme reentry conditions and landing with high precision. These systems open the door to new ways of testing, delivering, and operating at hypersonic speeds.

Inherently dual-use, our technology is built to meet urgent national security needs while laying the groundwork for future commercial applications. Backed by leading investors including Y Combinator, Spark Capital, and Lockheed Martin Ventures, and working with partners such as the U.S. Space Force and NASA, Inversion is pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in space-based defense and logistics.

What You'll Do

As the Senior Engineering Manager of Arc Vehicle Reentry
at Inversion, you will report directly to the Chief Engineer of Arc
. In this role, you will lead the multi-disciplinary engineers responsible for the aerothermal performance, primary structures, thermal protection systems (TPS), flap actuators, and hypersonic GNC algorithms of the Arc reentry vehicle.

Key Responsibilities

Lead daily operations, roadmaps, and budget allocation for the Arc Reentry organization, managing multiple teams across structures, GNC, flight sciences, and TPS production.
Own the technical delivery of the Arc primary vehicle structure, aerodynamic shape, and thermal protection system (TPS) integration.
Own the technical characterization of the aerodynamic forces and moments and aerothermal environments during hypersonic reentry.
Oversee the development, testing, and validation of Arc hypersonic reentry GNC algorithms and flight performance from reentry initiation through parachute deployment.
Coordinate with the centralized Reentry functional group to utilize core analysis tools for CFD aerothermal modeling, conjugate heat transfer, plasma modeling, and structural dynamics.
Manage the design, development, and qualification of high-temperature flap actuators and mechanism interfaces critical to hypersonic flight control.
Drive TPS production, tool design, and hands-on application processes for the physical vehicle build, collaborating directly with the Production and AI&T teams.
Recruit, mentor, and build a high-performance team, developing future engineering managers and technical leaders within the Reentry organization.
Lead critical multi-system trade studies, balancing mass budgets, thermal margins, aerodynamic control authority, and structural integrity.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or equivalent technical experience.
Typically 10+ years of technical experience in aerospace vehicle design, structural engineering, GNC, or aerothermodynamics.
Typically 3+ years of formal people-management experience, with a proven track record of leading multi-disciplinary engineering teams.
Deep technical competency in at least one core reentry field (aerothermal analysis, TPS development, hypersonic flight dynamics, or structural design).
Proven experience managing complex aerospace programs through design, environmental qualification, and flight operations.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to drive alignment across hardware, software, and production organizations.
This position is on-site at Inversion HQ in Playa Vista, CA.
Must have the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government Secret/Top Secret security clearance.

Desired Qualifications

Master's or Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
Direct experience with hypersonic flight systems, reentry vehicle architectures, or high-temperature structural actuation.
Familiarity with TPS materials characterization, structural bonding, and advanced composite fabrication.
Prior experience in a fast-paced startup environment.

Our office headquarters is located in Playa Vista, CA. This position requires in office presence.

Nu’s impact has been recognized in multiple awards, including Time 100 Most Influential Companies, Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies, and Forbes World’s Best Banks.

Visit our Institutional Page

About The Team

This role sits within Global Platforms Engineering: Engineering Enablement
, under Eric Young
(CTO, Global Platforms Engineering). The AI Developer Experience (AIDE) pillar is the AI-native counterpart to the separately led Developer Infrastructure pillar: a standing topic in CTO org-design reviews.

Reports to a Senior Director, Engineering Enablement and dotted line to Rahul Ahlawat
, Engineering Senior Director & Chief of Staff to the CTO. Leads a team of approximately 10–15 engineers today, spanning five workstreams, scaling with 8 committed "Deep Forge" headcounts plus external hiring. This is green-field scope with established backing: the charter, budget conversations, and headcount pipeline already exist. The Director shapes execution and strategy, not just strategy alone, and has real decision-making authority over team structure, build-vs-buy calls, and workstream prioritization. The Director will also engage directly with third-party AI vendors (e.g., Factory.ai, Devin-class tools) and with ICs across the five core workstreams.

About The Role

Nubank is one of the few companies with the scale (3,500+ engineers), AI ambition, and executive air cover to build a genuinely AI-native developer experience: not a bolt-on pilot. This role is responsible for defining and leading the AI Developer Experience pillar within Engineering Enablement, transforming how Nubank's engineers write, review, deploy, and operate software.

The Director inherits a mandate, a growing team, and a seat at the table with the CTO. The pillar already has real momentum: an early production win in the Vector agentic coding platform, an urgent context-infrastructure buildout, and direct executive sponsorship.

Key Responsibilities And Expectations

Own and scale the AI Developer Experience pillar, with an initial focus on measurably increasing shipped PRs per engineer per week through automation, and improving token efficiency as AI spend scales.

Build the team from the ground up, converting today's borrowed, part-time contributors into a dedicated, full-time organization; the CTO has personally committed to reallocating direct reports and unlocking headcount.

Run the build-vs-partner motion: stand up fast, structured engagements with third parties to benchmark, accelerate, and in some cases co-build: while defining objective eval criteria so decisions aren't subjective.

Core Workstreams

NuContext: the knowledge and context-extraction layer (docs, Confluence, Jira, code) that everything else depends on; currently the single highest-priority area for Nubank's long-term AI strategy. Owns ontology definition, context curation standards, knowledge graph traversal/retrieval, and context update mechanisms.
Vector (agentic coding & hosted environment): sandboxing, harness, memory/retrieval, and system-prompt optimization for AI-assisted coding.
Agentic Code Review: AI-assisted PR review to cut defect rates and cycle time, a direct lever on the org's top-line change failure rate (CFR) goal.
AI SRE: moving from vendor evaluation to AI-native incident detection, diagnosis, and remediation at scale.
Prompt Classification & Model Routing and 3rd-party AI tooling vendor management: scope and placement still being finalized; the Director will help shape this boundary.
Longer term, the AI Enablement Platform (routing, marketplace, authentication) is expected to fold into this scope as leadership bandwidth allows.

Qualifications

Professional Experience & Education
:

Proven leadership of AI-native developer tooling or platform teams, ideally at a company operating at meaningful engineering scale.
Track record building full-time, dedicated engineering teams out of fragmented, part-time, or borrowed resourcing: including experience in allocating teams, stellar in people leadership to do it without burning teams out.
Real experience structuring and running third-party vendor partnerships (evaluation, integration, managing lock-in risk) alongside first-party build.
Hands-on technical credibility in agentic coding systems, context/retrieval infrastructure, or developer-facing AI tooling: able to go deep with ICs, not just manage from a distance.
Comfort operating in a high-velocity, ambiguous, and high-executive-visibility organization; ability to align and mobilize teams to take on new challenges and scale impact.
High accountability and ownership mindset, coupled with the ability to move fast under pressure.
Comfort with an honest, unsolved problem space: even leading peer companies are far from 100% AI-authored code; this role is about the challenge and the resourcing to attack it, not a pre-solved problem.
A track record that positions the Director as the natural next-step candidate for the broader Engineering Enablement M6 role.
A builder's instinct for evaluation rigor: experience designing evals/benchmarks that replace subjective quality judgments with objective, repeatable measurement.
Experience with sandboxed agentic execution environments, retrieval-augmented systems, or LLM-based code review tooling (nice-to-have).
Familiarity with token-cost management as AI spend scales (nice-to-have).
Prior exposure to fintech, regulated environments, or large legacy codebases where AI adoption is harder to get right (nice-to-have).

Core Leadership Skills

The following executive leadership skills serve as a reference for senior leadership levels at Nubank, setting expectations that grow with increasing complexity, ambiguity, and influence.

BUSINESS ACUMEN

Drives strategic business alignment at Nubank by analyzing market dynamics, identifying opportunities, and ensuring informed decision-making to influence organizational direction.

COMMUNICATION

Masters complex communication, mentoring others, fostering open dialogue, and adapting strategies to enhance organizational effectiveness.

AGILE ADAPTABILITY

Leads with agility, pioneering solutions, fostering a culture of learning, collaboration, and continuous value delivery.

Role Location

Palo Alto, US: adhering to company policy for in-office attendance (2026: 2x/week; 2027 onwards: 3x/week).

jobs.title: Director of Engineering Operations
jobs.description:
Director of Engineering Operations
Location:
Milpitas, California

Position Summary
ScaleFlux is seeking an experienced Director of Engineering Operations
to serve as the principal business and operations leader for the Engineering organization and the trusted operational partner to the VP of Engineering.
This is a highly strategic leadership position responsible for building and scaling the operational foundation of a world-class fabless semiconductor engineering organization. The Director of Engineering Operations will lead engineering business operations, commercial and contract engagement, vendor management, engineering procurement, infrastructure planning, operational governance, and executive reporting.
The successful candidate will work closely with Engineering, Finance, Procurement, Legal, IT, Sales, Product Management, and executive leadership to ensure engineering teams have the tools, infrastructure, vendor partnerships, and operational support needed to successfully deliver innovative semiconductor products.
This is not
a Technical Program Management or Project Management role. Project execution is owned by engineering managers and program managers. This role focuses on enabling engineering excellence through strategic planning, operational leadership, business management, and cross-functional execution.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic Partner to the VP of Engineering
Serve as the trusted operational advisor and business partner to the VP of Engineering.
Drive strategic initiatives that improve engineering efficiency, scalability, and operational excellence.
Represent the Engineering organization in executive-level cross-functional initiatives.
Lead special projects on behalf of Engineering leadership.

Engineering Business Operations
Lead annual engineering operating plans, including:

OPEX planning and forecasting
CAPEX planning
Headcount planning
Budget tracking and variance analysis
Develop executive dashboards, KPIs, and business metrics to support engineering leadership.
Identify operational risks and recommend mitigation strategies.
Drive continuous improvement across engineering operations.

Engineering Contracts & Commercial Engagement
Lead engineering participation in commercial and technical contract discussions.
Partner with Legal, Procurement, Sales, and Engineering to negotiate technical and business terms.
Coordinate engineering review and approval for:

Customer engineering agreements
Evaluation agreements
Statements of Work (SOW)
Engineering service agreements
EDA software agreements
Semiconductor IP licensing agreements
Technology partnership agreements
Ensure engineering commitments are technically achievable, clearly documented, and aligned with business objectives.

Vendor Management & Engineering Procurement
Lead strategic sourcing and procurement activities for engineering organizations.
Responsibilities include:
EDA software
Semiconductor IP
Engineering software tools
Cloud infrastructure
Compute resources
Engineering development platforms
FPGA prototyping systems
Validation equipment
Laboratory equipment
Engineering services

Partner with Engineering and Procurement to:
Define technical requirements
Evaluate vendors
Coordinate technical assessments
Support commercial negotiations
Manage software renewals
Optimize engineering investments
Build long-term strategic supplier relationships

Engineering Infrastructure Strategy
Work with Engineering, CAD, IT, and Infrastructure teams to develop long-term infrastructure strategies supporting engineering growth.
Examples include:
Compute farms
AI compute clusters
Storage infrastructure
Engineering servers
Lab infrastructure
Validation systems
FPGA prototyping platforms
Network infrastructure

Support long-term capacity planning and technology roadmaps.

Process Governance & Operational Excellence
Develop standardized operational processes across the Engineering organization.
Examples include:
Engineering procurement workflows
Vendor onboarding
Contract review process
Engineering approval workflows
Design Change Notice (DCN) process
Engineering service request workflow
Engineering operational policies

Drive adoption and continuous improvement of engineering systems including:
Jira
Confluence
Jira Service Management
Other engineering productivity tools

Cross-functional Leadership
Partner closely with:
Engineering
Finance
Legal
Procurement
IT
HR
Product Management
Sales
Executive Leadership

Act as Engineering’s primary operational representative across the company.

Qualifications
Required
Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline.
10+ years of experience within the semiconductor industry.
Minimum 5 years of experience in a fabless semiconductor company.
Demonstrated experience supporting semiconductor engineering organizations.
Strong understanding of the ASIC product development lifecycle, including architecture, RTL development, verification, silicon bring-up, validation, product engineering, manufacturing, and production release.
Experience leading engineering business operations, vendor management, procurement, or engineering operational functions.
Experience working with EDA vendors, semiconductor IP providers, foundries, and technology partners.
Experience participating in engineering contract negotiations and commercial discussions.
Strong understanding of engineering budgeting, forecasting, and operational planning.
Exceptional analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written, verbal, and executive presentation skills.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional organizations without direct authority.

Preferred
MBA or master’s degree in engineering or business.
Experience with leading EDA vendors including Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA, Ansys, or similar.
Experience working with major semiconductor foundries such as TSMC, Samsung Foundry, UMC, or GlobalFoundries.
Experience with semiconductor IP licensing and technology partnerships.
Familiarity with engineering collaboration platforms including Jira, Confluence, and Jira Service Management.
Professional proficiency in English is required. Professional proficiency in Mandarin Chinese is highly desirable to facilitate collaboration with engineering teams, foundry partners, IP providers, and vendors across Asia.

Leadership Characteristics
The successful candidate will demonstrate:
Executive presence and sound business judgment.
Strong commercial acumen and negotiation skills.
High integrity and ownership.
Excellent relationship-building and communication skills.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with operational execution.
Strong analytical and financial mindset.
Ability to simplify complex operational challenges.
Passion for building scalable engineering organizations.

Within the first 12 months, the Director of Engineering Operations is expected to:
Establish a scalable engineering business operating model.
Improve visibility into engineering budgets, investments, and operational metrics.
Build standardized processes for engineering procurement, contracts, and operational governance.
Strengthen strategic relationships with EDA, IP, foundry, and technology partners.
Optimize engineering infrastructure planning to support company growth.
Become the trusted operational partner to the VP of Engineering and a respected leader across the organization.

Why Join ScaleFlux
This is a unique opportunity to build and shape the operational foundation of a fast-growing semiconductor company. Reporting directly to the VP of Engineering, you will play a critical leadership role in enabling engineering innovation, driving operational excellence, and supporting the successful delivery of next generation semiconductor products.

SOLV Energy is a leading provider of infrastructure services to the power industry, designing, building and maintaining utility scale solar, battery storage and high voltage substation projects nationwide.

Job Description Summary:

The Director of Engineering, Energy Storage leads, mentors, and develops SOLV Energy’s Energy Storage Engineering team. Oversees the design of energy storage systems for utility-scale renewable energy projects, ensuring compliance with technical standards, safety regulations, and project requirements. Drives innovation, implements value engineering strategies, and maintains quality and reliability across all energy storage deliverables.

This role can be fully remote or hybrid, with regular in-office presence in San Diego, CA. Up to 50% travel is required. Specific location details and expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

Job Description:

This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned

Position Responsibilities and Duties:

Department Management/Leadership

Hire, manage, and mentor a diverse team of engineers, focused on energy storage systems and design.
Foster effective communication and collaboration between the Energy Storage Engineering group and cross-functional teams, including internal and external engineers, business development managers, project managers, pre-construction managers, procurement specialists, schedulers, estimators, and construction teams.
Allocate resources effectively to meet project deadlines and ensure optimal team utilization.
Overall management and responsibility of SOLV Energy Storage Engineering team, including establishing and maintaining department goals, budgets, and performance metrics.

Develop innovative, customer-centric engineering solutions that address client needs, reduce cost, and enhance project value.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Perception
jobs.description:
The Company

Saildrone is a maritime defense company and the global leader in autonomous unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). With more ocean miles and real-world operational experience than any USV manufacturer or operator, Saildrone maintains active, combat-deployed systems supporting national security and force projection around the world, 24/7/365.

Saildrone’s manufacturing and R&D headquarters are located in Alameda, CA, with business development and sales operations in Washington, DC, and deployment hubs in Europe and the Middle East. By combining proven autonomous operations, edge computing, advanced sensing, renewable power, and the most advanced and robust unmanned surface technology on the planet, Saildrone is shaping how the Navy of the future operates. Join a fast-moving, mission-driven team at the forefront of maritime security and autonomous innovation.

THE POSITION

Saildrone is seeking a Senior Engineering Manager, Perception to join our Robotics Software Org. Reporting directly to the Director, Robotics Software, you will play a critical role in architecting, implementing, and productionizing our next-gen perception software to our drone fleet. We are looking for a technical leader who creates clarity from ambiguity and has a proven track record of independently driving execution in a fast-paced environment. In this role, you will balance strategic people management with deep technical ownership, staying hands-on with architecture and code while steering a world-class team of autonomy engineers.

THE TEAM

The Perception Engineering Team is responsible for designing and deploying advanced sensing and perception capabilities that power Saildrone's autonomous operations. We are focused on delivering robust and scalable solutions for global maritime domain awareness to safeguard our uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs) and provide mission-critical data in a national security and defense environment. Our team processes petabytes of unique, multi-modal ocean data collected across millions of nautical miles, solving the complex visual challenges of tracking targets amidst massive wave clutter, severe vehicle motion, and changing atmospheric conditions.

The Responsibilities

Lead and scale an elite engineering team, providing high-impact technical mentorship and career development while remaining directly hands-on with core architecture, code reviews, and critical implementations.
Be accountable for the delivery, reliability, and edge performance of real-time perception software running on uncrewed platforms during months-long ocean deployments.
Partner with the Autonomy, Machine Learning, Systems, and Hardware teams to align on product roadmaps, manage cross-functional dependencies, and ensure seamless sensor-to-actuation integration.
Drive day-to-day execution using C++, our state-of-the-art robotics perception and ML software, and agile methodologies to maintain high-velocity development cycles and rigorous production-grade standards.
Proactively identify system bottlenecks, algorithmic risks, and team blockers, implementing strategic mitigations to optimize high-performance compute on embedded platforms (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson).
Establish robust validation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing, and simulation frameworks leveraging large-scale maritime datasets to guarantee deterministic safety and performance.

The Qualifications

Experience: 8+ years of progressive software experience in robotics, drones, or autonomous driving, with at least 2+ years of direct engineering management or technical leadership experience.
Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Hands-on Expertise: Strong technical depth in modern C++ (14/17/20) and production-grade software development for Linux embedded environments, with the ability to dive into the codebase, review code, and make sound technical judgments
Domain Knowledge: Deep understanding of perception fundamentals, including multi-object tracking, 3D computer vision, multi-sensor calibration, or deep learning deployment at the edge.
Sensors & Fusion: Proven experience working with complex maritime sensor stacks, integrating and fusing raw data from long-range cameras, marine Radar, LiDAR, and AIS electronics.
Dataset Management: Experience building ingestion pipelines, auto-labeling frameworks, or regression workflows optimized for petabyte-scale, edge-case-heavy dataset exploration.
Leadership Style: Ability to dive into technical codebases to unblock developers while maintaining a highly collaborative, inclusive, and mission-driven engineering culture.

Physical Requirements

Office & Tech Work: Work is primarily performed on a computer and requires the ability to operate a keyboard and peripheral devices.
Onsite Collaboration: Ability to maintain a hybrid schedule, including traveling to and working out of our Alameda waterfront headquarters 3 days per week.
Hardware-in-the-Loop Interaction: Occasional need to collaborate closely with the hardware team in laboratory or dock environments, including standing, bending, and light handling of test payloads or sensors up to 30 lbs.

The base salary range for this position is shown below. Actual compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and qualifications. This range reflects the base salary for candidates in states requiring pay transparency disclosure.

Salary Range

$259,649—$305,469 USD

To view Saildrone's candidate privacy policy, please visit: https://www.saildrone.com/privacy-policy.

Benefits

At Saildrone, we’re building operational capability that matters—and that requires people who can do their best work over the long term. We invest in our team’s well-being, financial security, and professional growth so you can focus on delivering real-world impact with confidence and stability. Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support you and your family while you contribute to a mission with lasting significance.

Generous Time Off: Competitive Paid Time Off (PTO) accrual plus a robust annual holiday schedule and paid sick leave ensure you can rest, reset, and sustain performance over time.
Comprehensive Health Coverage: Premium, multi-tier Medical, Dental, and Vision plans with significant company contributions for employees and dependents—providing security and peace of mind.
Shared Ownership in the Mission: Equity grants are a core part of our compensation, allowing you to participate in the long-term value you help create through meaningful, operational work.
Retirement Savings: Access to a 401(k) retirement plan with flexible pre-tax and Roth payroll contribution options supports long-term financial planning.
Investment in Your Growth: We support your continuous learning through an annual professional development reimbursement program, empowering you to sharpen your skills and stay ahead of the curve in a rapidly evolving field.
Relocation Support: For eligible roles, we offer relocation assistance to help bring the world’s best talent to our mission-critical locations.

Saildrone is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

. Minimum qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience
15 years of experience in software engineering, with 8 years of experience in a technical engineering role
Experience with protecting systems
Experience in vulnerability management, posture management, or risk analysis

Preferred qualifications:

Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science
Experience motivating others to act by creating a shared sense of outlook or purpose, creating a compelling roadmap for the future, communicating clearly, and employing a collaborative leadership approach
Experience leading complex cross-functional engineering projects

Experience providing clarity and alignment across the organization on goals, outcomes, and timelines as well as encouraging engineering excellence and coaching
Entrepreneurial and strategic mindset, growing at the intersection of technology and business with broad technical experience

About The Job

As the Director of Engineering for Product Security (Safe Coding, Cryptography, and Software Supply Chain) in Privacy, Safety, and Security (PSS), you will lead a 100-person global organization across the US, Zurich, and Singapore. You will define the strategic outlook and own the infrastructure responsible for building Google’s secure-by-design development platforms and code integrity systems, ensuring our core software remains resilient at scale.

In this role, you will drive defensive security into the AI era by transitioning Google from reactive vulnerability remediation to automated, secure-by-construction systems. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

Technology Planning & Execution

Systems & Infrastructure

Continuously evaluate opportunities to streamline operations

Ensure systems and data protection without overengineering
Maintain compliance with standard industry practices

Increased system adoption and satisfaction

Measurable ROI on technology investments
Successful implementation of automation initiatives

Experience implementing automation or workflow improvements

jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Energy Storage
jobs.description:
SOLV Energy is a leading provider of infrastructure services to the power industry, designing, building and maintaining utility scale solar, battery storage and high voltage substation projects nationwide.

Job Description Summary:

The Director of Engineering, Energy Storage leads, mentors, and develops SOLV Energy’s Energy Storage Engineering team. Oversees the design of energy storage systems for utility-scale renewable energy projects, ensuring compliance with technical standards, safety regulations, and project requirements. Drives innovation, implements value engineering strategies, and maintains quality and reliability across all energy storage deliverables.

This role can be fully remote or hybrid, with regular in-office presence in San Diego, CA. Up to 50% travel is required. Specific location details and expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

Job Description:

This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned

Position Responsibilities and Duties:

Department Management/Leadership

Hire, manage, and mentor a diverse team of engineers, focused on energy storage systems and design.
Foster effective communication and collaboration between the Energy Storage Engineering group and cross-functional teams, including internal and external engineers, business development managers, project managers, pre-construction managers, procurement specialists, schedulers, estimators, and construction teams.
Allocate resources effectively to meet project deadlines and ensure optimal team utilization.
Overall management and responsibility of SOLV Energy Storage Engineering team, including establishing and maintaining department goals, budgets, and performance metrics.
Establish and maintain partnerships with a diverse group of third-party Engineers-of-Record (EORs).
Represent SOLV Engineering and management in customer and client meetings.

Technical Oversight

Oversee development of Energy Storage engineering standards and procurement specifications.
Implement and maintain quality control processes to ensure designs comply with all owner, SOLV, AHJ, and vendor requirements.
Proactively identify and resolve potential design and construction challenges and coordinate with various stakeholders to develop cost-effective solutions.
Lead design efforts for interconnection systems, including coordinating utility approvals, ISO and NERC compliance, and energization plans.

Strategic Initiatives

Drive adoption of new technologies and best practices to optimize system performance, reliability, and cost.
Develop innovative, customer-centric engineering solutions that address client needs, reduce cost, and enhance project value.
Represent SOLV Energy team as a technical subject matter expert (SME) during client interviews/meetings as required.
Stay informed on industry best practices and technological advancements in utility-scale energy storage design.
Stay informed on relevant regulations, codes, and guidelines that may impact future SOLV project designs.
Provide SME guidance/consultation to other departments within SOLV, as needed.
Training and Development
Identify training and development needs and provide opportunities for skills enhancement and professional growth.
Develop and mentor staff for career advancement.

Minimum Skills or Experience Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (preferred).
10+ years of experience in engineering with a focus on Energy Storage, renewables, or power systems in an EPC or Owner/Engineer environment.
Minimum 5+ years of experience in management
Professional Engineer (PE) license is preferred.
Ability to travel up to 50% of the time will be needed.
Proven track record of successfully designing and delivering utility-scale Energy Storage projects.
Strong technical background in protection and control systems, relay settings, and NERC compliance.
Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary teams and working in a fast-paced environment.
Technical subject matter expert of applicable codes and standards (NEC, IEEE, IBC, ASCE, NESC, NFPA, utility standards) is preferred.
Extensive experience with grid operations and regulatory requirements (FERC Order 841, IEEE 1547) is preferred.
Strong understanding of fire protection requirements (UL9540, UL9540A, NFPA855).
Deep knowledge of EPC engineering workflows, including design deliverables, submittals, document control, and coordination with engineering partners 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal
Strong leadership, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
Strong sense of urgency.
Ability to travel extensively throughout the United States, up to 50% of the time.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without requiring employer sponsorship now or in the future.

jobs.title: Director of Technology Development
jobs.description:
Department:
RENU - SQI Regenerative Eng

Salary/Grade:
EXS/12

Job Summary

The Querrey Simpson Institute for Regenerative Engineering (QSI RENU) is a new Institute for engineering in medicine and healthcare innovation established to foster, develop, and disseminate engineering-driven technology innovations that restore tissue and organ function to improve patient care and quality of life. The mission of this new institute predominantly integrates the talents of Northwestern University faculty from McCormick School of Engineering and Feinberg School of Medicine to create convergence research, education, and innovation ecosystem to develop enabling tools for preserving, restoring, and augmenting tissue and organ function. Staff within the Institute support this mission and are an integral part of the Institute’s success.

QSI RENU has an opening for a Director of Technology Development who will report to QSI RENU’s Director. This position acts as Director of Technology Development and will be responsible for implementing strategic initiatives for translational research for QSI RENU. This individual will be responsible for building and managing institute scientific/technical infrastructure, supporting the execution of internally and externally funded research programs via project management, coordinating operational research budgets, operating RENU’s GMP facility and other institute core facilities on NU downtown campus, supporting tech transfer of processes to cGMP manufacturing, including developing and reviewing standard operating procedures (SOP), protocols, and technical reports, assisting with design and delivery of training courses, overseeing business development activities including marketing the facilities, building relationship with sponsors, attracting and retaining clients, and submitting grants to support the facilities. An ideal candidate should have a technical background that enables them to implement RENU’s mission, oversee research operations, and maintain a compliant GMP facility, supporting clients, as necessary.

Specific Responsibilities

Strategic and Translational Research Initiatives

Implement institute-wide strategic initiatives for translational research.
Support internally and externally funded research programs.
Assist with new grant proposals.

Research Infrastructure and Facility Management

Build, operate, and manage scientific and technical infrastructure.
Oversee day-to-day operations of GMP and other lab facilities.
Purchase and manage lab and core facility equipment.
Support client onboarding and client audits.

Research Project Management

Provide project management for funded research (coordinate meetings, progress/technical reports).
Develop and coordinate operational and research budgets.
Manage large teams to achieve specific milestones and timelines.

Regulatory Compliance and Quality Systems

Operate and maintain a compliant GMP facility.
Support tech transfer of processes to cGMP manufacturing.
Develop, review, and deliver SOPs, technical reports, and training protocols.
Ensure compliance with relevant regulations (21CFR, ICH Q guidelines).

Business Development and External Engagement

Market institute facilities and services.
Build and maintain relationships with sponsors, clients, and external partners.
Attract and retain clients for the GMP facility.
Develop and execute a business plan for the GMP facility.

Supervision, Training and Education

Supervise 2 staff members, and mentors staff members.
Assist with the design and delivery of GMP training courses.
Development and delivery of SOP and training protocols

Miscellaneous

Performs other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Technical background with an undergraduate degree in science, engineering, or related field
5-8 years of experience in a GMP regulated field under 21CFR 210, 211, 820, and ICH Q&
Experience with federally sponsored grant proposals (such as DoE, DoD, NSF), evidence of developing professional and fruitful relationships with research funding entities, a demonstrated track record of successfully orchestrating and encouraging faculty members to work together to secure large grants.
Demonstrated Experience operating GMP facility.
Demonstrated Experience managing a large team with specific milestones and timelines.
Experimental design experience.
Experience leading a project team.

Preferred Qualifications
