jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager (Network Value + Outcomes)
jobs.description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access.
We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

Senior Engineering Manager, Payer & Outcomes

Headway's mission is a big one – to build a new mental health care system everyone can access. We've built technology that helps people find great therapists with the first software-enabled national network of providers accepting insurance.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but the majority of providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway is building a new mental healthcare system that everyone can access by making it easy for therapists to accept insurance and scale their practice.

Headway was founded in 2019. Since then, we've grown into a diverse, national network of over 60,000 mental healthcare providers across all 50 states who run their practice on our software and have served over 1 million patients. We're a Series D company with over $325m in funding from a16z (Andreessen Horowitz), Accel, GV (formerly Google Ventures), Spark Capital, Thrive Capital, Forerunner Ventures and Health Care Service Corporation.

We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About Engineering At Headway

Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!).

Principles That Guide Us

Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they're facing.
Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iterating.
Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.
Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

Tools We Use

Languages: Python 3, TypeScript
Libraries & Frameworks: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, React, Remix, Next.js
Datastores: Postgres, Redis
Infrastructure: AWS (Fargate, ECS, S3, SageMaker and more), Spark and Kafka
Monitoring: Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry
Version Control: Github
Vulnerability Management: Snyk, Semgrep
Cloud Security: Lacework

About This Role

Headway's mission is to build a new mental healthcare system that everyone can access, one that works for patients, providers, and payers alike. Our Payer & Outcomes group is where we prove that model works. We build the systems that answer two questions insurers have never been able to answer well: did the care actually work, and was it worth it?

As Senior Engineering Manager for Payer & Outcomes, you'll lead the two teams that answer them. Outcomes builds our measurement backbone: collecting patient-reported outcomes at scale, tracking symptom improvement and retention to care, and turning that into evidence we can stand behind. Network Value builds the intelligence behind utilization and cost of care, covering patient acuity and segmentation, provider efficiency ranking, and the sub-network logic that routes a patient to the right level of care.

These two teams share data foundations, a measurement stack, and an audience, which is why they sit together under one leader. You'll own delivery on a company-level goal we have publicly committed to: significantly increasing the share of new patients with a baseline outcome measure, without increasing provider churn. That means holding quality and adoption in tension rather than trading one for the other.

You'll grow and mentor a team of roughly eight engineers plus an engineering manager, set the technical and operational roadmap across both pods, and partner daily with Product, Clinical, Data Science, and our payer-facing commercial teams. This is a deeply cross-functional role: your work is what lets Headway move payers from administrative oversight to genuine care partnership.

The stakes here are concrete. Elsewhere in the group we now review clinical notes and prompt providers to put a safety plan in place when a patient shows signs of suicidal risk. At full adoption across our network, that single intervention is estimated to prevent more than 1,000 deaths a year. Your teams build the measurement and targeting layer that decides where interventions like that get aimed, and whether we can prove they worked.

Who You Are

We're looking for an experienced engineering leader who is product-minded, data-informed, and energized by growth. You'll work closely with Engineering Leadership, Product, and Data to shape the future of Headway's payer strategy. There is an unusually direct line from your team's work to whether this model of care survives contact with the market.

In this role you will

Lead, manage, and grow two engineering teams
Own delivery on a company-level outcomes key result, including its guardrails
Set the technical and operational roadmap across measurement, segmentation, and utilization
Develop your team through weekly 1:1s, mentorship, and direct feedback, and develop the manager reporting to you
Partner closely with Product, Clinical, Data Science, and Commercial to iterate quickly and rigorously
Contribute to the broader group and company strategy, not just your own roadmap

Experience We're Seeking

6+ years of engineering management experience at a high-growth startup or scale-up, including managing managers or tech leads
3–5+ years of experience as a software engineer, enough to hold technical direction credibly
A track record of building and leading high-performing teams that delivered business outcomes through technical investment
A strong product mindset and cross-functional relationships that build trust with users and stakeholders
Experience owning an externally-committed metric, with the scope discipline that requires
Comfort with data- and ML-heavy systems: measurement, experimentation, and metric guardrails
Nice to have: healthcare, insurance, or another regulated, high-trust domain
Nice to have: value-based care, quality measurement, or utilization management
Nice to have: prior experience with Python, React, and AWS infrastructure

You'll love this role if you want to

Lead the teams that decide whether a new model of mental healthcare can be proven, not just described
Own a number the company reports externally, with the autonomy that comes with it
Build an engineering management layer beneath you rather than inherit a finished org

Our interview process

After you apply to Headway, here are some details of what to expect during the interview process.

Initial screen: You'll connect with someone in recruiting so you can learn more about the team, Headway's mission and exciting growth, and we can get a better idea of your background.
First rounds: You'll meet with an engineering leader on the team to go deeper into your team and people leadership experience. You'll also complete an AI Coding round — a collaborative session where we're less focused on syntax and more on how you think through problems and work with AI tools in a technical context.
Final rounds: You'll meet team members across product and engineering leadership for multiple behavioral interviews and one more technical interview (System Design), leaving you with a fuller picture of what it's like to work at Headway.
References and the Offer: Our favorite part of the process! We'll send over all of the details, including specifics on employee equity, and congratulatory messages from excited future team members!

Compensation And Benefits

The expected base pay range for this position is $265,200 - 331,500, based on a variety of factors including qualifications, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for performance-based variable compensation and an equity grant, depending on the position and level.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
About Buildout

Buildout is the AI deal engine for CRE brokerages, automating every step from first contact to commission. While brokers focus on relationships and winning listings, Buildout handles the workflows behind the scenes, turning manual processes into intelligent, scalable systems. Trusted by over 50,000 brokers, Buildout powers more profitable deals from lead to close. Learn more at www.buildout.com.

The Opportunity

Buildout is hiring a Director of Engineering to lead the performance and execution of our engineering organization. You’ll manage a team of engineers and technical leads, creating the clarity, accountability, and support they need to do their best work. You will own the people and operating systems behind a healthy engineering organization, from coaching and performance management to staffing, planning, delivery, and cross-functional partnership. You’ll help the team thoughtfully adopt AI-assisted development practices that improve developer productivity, software quality, and delivery speed.

This role is an important partner to our SVP of Engineering. While the SVP of Engineering remains focused on technology strategy, architecture, and long-term direction, you will turn that direction into an effective, predictable, and high-performing engineering operation.

What You'll Own

Engineering Leadership & Talent

Lead the day-to-day performance and development of our engineering organization, making sure every engineer knows what good looks like, where they stand, and how they can grow.
Manage and coach engineers and technical leads, giving them the context and support to make good decisions without needing you in the middle of every one.
Recognize and grow strong performers, develop future technical leaders, and address performance concerns directly and early.
Own engineering hiring and onboarding, building the talent and team structure we need to meet the needs of the business.

Delivery & Operational Excellence

Create clear accountability for engineering delivery across teams, with enough structure to make execution predictable without slowing people down.
Maintain a clear view of capacity, commitments, dependencies, and risk so problems surface early and leadership isn't surprised.
Step into cross-team dependencies, competing priorities, and delivery challenges when teams need help getting unstuck.
Use AI as a force multiplier for the engineering organization, setting clear expectations for adoption and turning what works into repeatable practices across coding, testing, documentation, automation, and the broader development lifecycle.
Drive measurable improvements in developer productivity and team effectiveness while maintaining strong standards for software quality and responsible AI use.

Product & Business Partnership

Serve as Product's primary partner for engineering execution, bringing a clear view of capacity, feasibility, risk, and tradeoffs into roadmap and prioritization decisions.
Help turn product priorities into realistic engineering commitments—and make the tradeoffs clear when everything can't be a priority.
Communicate risks early and honestly, bringing problems forward with enough context to make good decisions.
Be a steady escalation point when delivery, staffing, or organizational issues cross team boundaries or don't have an obvious answer.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 Days:

Learn the Organization

Build trust with engineers, technical leads, Product, and executive stakeholders.
Understand team structures, responsibilities, delivery processes, and technical ownership.
Learn existing strengths, bottlenecks, and organizational pain points.
Observe planning, delivery, and cross-functional interactions before making major changes.

Establish Leadership Presence

Begin regular one-on-ones with all direct reports.
Understand individual career goals, concerns, and performance histories.
Build credibility as a leader who listens, follows through, and removes obstacles.

First 90 Days:

Become The Primary Operational Leader

Become the first point of escalation for delivery and personnel issues.
Establish visibility into delivery risks, team health, and organizational capacity.
Build strong working relationships with Product leadership.
Create consistency in communication and expectations across teams.

Identify Organizational Improvements

Recommend targeted improvements to execution, planning, staffing, or team structure.
Clarify ownership boundaries where necessary.
Ensure technical leads are focused on technical leadership rather than people-management responsibilities.

First 6 Months:

Improve Organizational Execution

Delivery risks are identified and addressed proactively.
Cross-team dependencies are managed effectively.
Product views the Director as the primary engineering execution partner.
Engineers receive consistent coaching, feedback, and career development.

Reduce SVP of Engineering Operational Involvement

Personnel issues are handled without SVP of Engineering intervention.
Delivery escalations are routed through the Director.
Team-level execution concerns are resolved without executive involvement.
The SVP of Engineering is spending significantly less time on organizational and operational concerns.

First Year:

Build a High-Performing Engineering Organization

Engineering delivery is predictable and transparent.
Strong accountability exists across teams without excessive process.
Performance management is consistent and effective.
High performers are identified, developed, and retained.
Underperformance is addressed quickly and professionally.

Enable the SVP of Engineering Role

The SVP of Engineering focuses primarily on technology strategy, architecture, executive leadership, and long-term planning.
The Director serves as the trusted operational leader of the engineering organization.
Engineering and Product leadership operate as effective partners.
The organization scales successfully without increasing executive involvement in day-to-day operations.

What Makes a Great Candidate

You make expectations unmistakable. People rarely leave a conversation with you wondering what matters, who owns what, or what happens next. You create clarity without turning every problem into a new process.
You make teams run better. You look for ways to make the team faster, more effective, and more consistent without adding unnecessary processes. You see AI as a force multiplier and know how to turn it from a tool into a meaningful part of how an engineering team builds, solves problems, and delivers.
You coach before you rescue. Your instinct is not to take over when someone struggles. You ask the right questions, give direct feedback, and help people build the judgment to solve the next problem themselves.
You can hold the line without hardening the room. You are comfortable addressing missed commitments, performance concerns, and difficult tradeoffs. You are direct without being careless and empathetic without avoiding accountability.
You see around corners. You notice when a staffing gap, unclear ownership boundary, or unresolved dependency is likely to become a larger problem. You raise it early and help the right people act before it becomes an emergency.
You translate between Product and Engineering. You can hear an ambitious product goal and identify the engineering choices beneath it. You help both sides understand capacity, risk, and tradeoffs.
You likely also have:
Experience leading and developing engineers across multiple product teams
Experience with performance management, hiring, and career development.
Experience leading technical leads and senior engineers
Enough technical depth to understand engineering tradeoffs and earn the trust of experienced developers, without needing to be the primary architect.
Demonstrated success improving organizational effectiveness while maintaining a strong engineering culture.

Location: This is a fully remote role open across most of the US.

Compensation: The targeted compensation range for this position is $160,000 - $180,000 plus bonus.

Reporting To: Alan Spadoni, our SVP, Engineering

Perks & Benefits

This program includes:

Impactful insurance and benefit options, including 2 medical plans to choose from, 100% coverage of employee dental and vision insurance premiums, HSA seed, company-paid STD, LTD, life insurance, and telemedicine, and a wellness benefit of $400/year.
Policies that support a healthy work/life harmony, including Flexible PTO, 14 paid company holidays, paid parental leave, and give back days
401(k) with 4% company match and immediate vesting
A fully remote work culture with a monthly remote work reimbursement ($600/year) to support our distributed team and an annual, in-person company kickoff
Challenging problems to solve with a committed and supportive team who are invested in your growth and development
A wonderfully quirky culture where you’re encouraged to bring your whole self to work

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access.
We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

Headway is building a new mental healthcare system that everyone can access by making it easy for therapists to accept insurance and scale their practice.

Version Control: Github
Vulnerability Management: Snyk, Semgrep
Cloud Security: Lacework

Headway's mission is to build a new mental healthcare system that everyone can access, one that works for patients, providers, and payers alike. Our Payer & Outcomes group is where we prove that model works. We build the systems that answer two questions insurers have never been able to answer well: did the care actually work, and was it worth it?

The Role

At Hadrian, data is part of the factory's operating system. The scheduler deciding what runs next, models predicting cycle time and demand, systems interpreting engineering drawings, analytics tracking production, and operators understanding what is happening on the floor all depend on the same thing: a trustworthy path from the physical and software systems that generate data to the teams and products that use it.

The Data Platform team owns that path. We build the shared infrastructure for ingestion and CDC, event streaming, the warehouse and lakehouse, orchestration, data contracts, quality, lineage, and the foundational data models that sit underneath Analytics, Data Science, Operations Research, ML, and operational software. Today that includes Snowflake, Iceberg on S3, PeerDB, Redpanda/Kafka, Dagster, dbt, Kubernetes, and protobuf/gRPC. Some of our data begins in conventional software systems. Some begins on CNC machines, inspection equipment, PLCs, engineering files, and the factory floor.

As an Senior Engineering Manager, you will build and lead the team responsible for making this platform reliable, coherent, and useful as Hadrian scales to many factories. You will own the people, execution, operating quality, and direction of the team while staying technically close enough to challenge architecture, understand failure modes, and help engineers make good tradeoffs.

What You’ll Do

Build the team and platform that become Hadrian's data backbone. Lead the engineers responsible for the path from machines and operational systems to the trusted datasets, streams, and interfaces that scheduling, analytics, ML, software, and factory operations depend on.
Own the Data Platform roadmap and delivery. Turn ambiguous needs across Software, Infrastructure, Analytics, Data Science, Operations Research, ML, and Manufacturing into clear priorities, interfaces, owners, and commitments.
Raise the operational bar for the platform: reliability, data-quality SLAs, observability, incident response, backfills and recovery, cost, security, schema evolution, provenance, and clear ownership when something fails.
Partner with senior engineers and technical leads on architecture across CDC and streaming, Snowflake and Iceberg, orchestration, data contracts, schema governance, and the interfaces between the data platform and its consumers. You do not need to design every system yourself, but you need the depth to ask the hard questions and recognize when important semantics or failure modes are missing.
Turn repeated one-off work into paved roads. Build standards, contracts, tooling, documentation, and migration paths that let other engineering and data teams move faster without creating a collection of bespoke pipelines.
Hire and grow an exceptional team. Set a clear technical and performance bar, give direct feedback, develop engineers into broader technical leaders, delegate real ownership, and build a team whose capability grows faster than its headcount.

What We’re Looking For

A track record leading engineers responsible for production data infrastructure, distributed systems, developer platforms, infrastructure, or similarly critical technical systems. For Senior EM, you have led multiple substantial workstreams or teams and developed senior technical leaders.
Strong technical judgment in modern data and platform systems: event streaming and CDC, warehouses and lakehouses, orchestration, schema evolution, data modeling, distributed-system failure modes, and the tradeoffs behind reliable data delivery.
Experience building for environments with real constraints. You understand that the architecture changes when data comes from hardware, machines, devices, files, telemetry, regulated systems, edge environments, or other sources that do not behave like a clean application database.
A real platform mindset. You think in shared abstractions, contracts, ownership, operating guarantees, adoption, migration, deprecation, and paved roads — not just a set of infrastructure components owned by one team.
An operator's mindset. You know what your systems promise, how you know they are healthy, what happens when those promises fail, and how an incident becomes a permanent improvement rather than a recurring story.
Strong people leadership and high agency across organizational boundaries. Your engineers know what is expected of them, where they stand, and how they can grow; when a dependency is blocking the team, you go resolve it rather than simply reporting it upward.

What Will Set You Apart

5+ years of management experience in manufacturing, semiconductors, hardware, robotics, autonomy, industrial systems, test/measurement, or edge computing, especially where the data platform had to bridge software with physical systems. Backgrounds from companies such as NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Xilinx, Altera, Qualcomm, Applied Materials, Lam Research, Tesla, Anduril, Shield AI, or similar environments are especially relevant.
Experience with heterogeneous data beyond application tables: telemetry, events, files, device identity, timestamps and clock drift, units, provenance, schema drift, deletes, late or out-of-order data, partial records, retries, and backfills.
Experience taking a data or infrastructure platform from an early working system to a broadly adopted internal product used by many teams.
Experience operating in security-sensitive or regulated environments such as aerospace, defense, FedRAMP, CMMC, or other environments where data governance and access control are part of the architecture.
A track record of building strong hiring and onboarding systems and helping senior engineers become effective technical leads, Staff+ engineers, or future managers.

Compensation

For this role, the target salary range is $249,000 -
$299,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

SaniSure is a high-growth multinational manufacturer of single-use products and systems used in the production of biological drugs, including cell therapies, gene therapies, and vaccines. With operations in the U.S. and Europe, we supply global pharmaceutical and biotech companies with the critical tools they need to develop and manufacture some of today's most innovative and life-changing medicines.

As we continue to expand our product offerings and global footprint, SaniSure offers an exciting opportunity to join a nimble, customer-focused company at the forefront of the biotech industry.

Job Summary

The Director of Engineering – Design is responsible for global product design at SaniSure. Scope includes assuring velocity and efficiency of drawing and Bill of Material throughput while maintaining accuracy and quality, tracking and managing associated key performance indicators (KPIs), selecting and deploying software, training, design tools, and design libraries, authoring and updating design SOPs and Work Instructions, engineering data integrity and data services, and the Engineering portions of product change control and change management, and urgently resolving design-related issues that impact production and end-customers.

Essential Functions

Manage the global team responsible for computer-aided design (CAD) at SaniSure. Set and continuously improve global CAD standards, templates, design libraries, and assure deployment and training.
Provide global leadership for deployment of 3D CAD and PDM. Work cross-functionally to build out the global data systems framework.
Develop deep product knowledge to provide technical design expertise to Sales, Customers, and other functional areas. Consult with other subject matter experts as required.
Review design requirements inputs from Customers, Sales, and Product Line Managers. Assure requirements are clearly translated into design features. Push for clarity and for closure of gaps in information.
Serve as the main point of Design contact for major customer Requests for Proposals (RFPs).
Analyze mechanical designs, including sketches, technical drawings, schematics, specifications and associated product measurements. Conduct risk assessments using FMEA framework, and drive risk mitigations as required. Lead design and drawing reviews as needed.
Promote the options for presenting alternative designs to customers, especially when it comes to products manufactured by SaniSure.
Assist engineering personnel with material sourcing for new parts in support of their designs.

Ensure full technical documentation of designs including BOMs, drawings, schematics, engineering change control, and procedures adhere to customer requirements, industry regulations, and quality standards.
Assure efficient prioritization and task management. Directly engage in ongoing oversight of turn-around-times for drawings and BOMs. Drive the global team to meet or exceed their objectives for established metrics and Targets To Improve (TTIs), especially time commitments, while maintaining accuracy.
Work with R&D, New Product Introduction, and with Manufacturing to integrate a Design for Manufacture & Assembly (DFMA) and Design to Cost (DTC) perspective.
Maintain organized and controlled records of all drawings and BOMs. Drive and facilitate assigned portions of product change management and control.
Own data integrity and data services when it comes to item master creation and curating assigned product data within SaniSure databases. This includes Product Data Management (PDM) and ERP.
Support product configuration management.
Develop and maintain positive rapport and working relationships with other personnel across the organization in support of initiatives to execute product improvements and enhancements.
Provide technical direction and guidance to less experienced Engineers and Drafters.
Provide inputs for departmental budgeting, and track and manage to assure spending stays within set parameters.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Bachelor's degree in Engineering; Master's preferred.

Minimum 10 years of overall Engineering experience.
Minimum 5 years in a former role managing a team of Engineers.
Experience with staffing, and with growing and developing strong teams. This includes active performance management.
Experience setting top-down department goals and objectives tied to business metrics and driving team performance in the context of business results.
Expert knowledge and demonstrated hands-on experience with Solidworks CAD software, both 3D and 2D.
Knowledge of plastic component and tool design, especially injection molding, and some blow molding.
Able to read and comprehend and interpret documents such as drawings, BOMs, blueprints, and operating procedures. Able to train and guide less experienced personnel on proper interpretation and best practices.
Advanced understanding of mathematical fundamentals of plane and solid geometry, fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.
Design control, change control, risk management experience (FMEA).
In depth knowledge of creation of 2D and 3D drawings and related Bill of Materials (BoMs).
Able to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.
Strong MS Office skills, including Excel.
Strong ERP knowledge, SyteLine preferred.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Patient, tactful, diplomatic, and approachable.
Able to represent SaniSure from a position of design expertise when customer-facing.
Able to stay calm in challenging situations.
Keen sense of urgency and ability to deliver ahead of deadlines.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Able to establish and maintain effective working relationships.
Able to effectively work in a fast-paced environment and frequently manage multiple priorities.
Must be self-motivated, amendable to a variety of work projects and work efficiently independently and as part of a team.
Excellent follow-up skills.

This organization builds the products and platforms behind LendingTree's consumer experience — the marketplace journeys consumers move through, the logged-in account experience they return to, the recommendation and personalization capabilities that guide them, and the integrations that connect LendingTree to the lenders, servicers, and data partners powering it all.

About the Role

LendingTree is hiring a Director of Engineering to lead a multi-team engineering organization responsible for our consumer-facing products and the platforms behind them. You'll own the engineering strategy, guide architecture and delivery across your portfolio, and you'll be accountable for the technical health, velocity, and reliability of everything your teams ship.

This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role. You'll partner with Product, Design, Data Science, and Business stakeholders to shape the roadmap, and you'll be a senior voice on how we build — architecture, engineering standards, platform investment, and talent. Your portfolio will include ownership of the logged-in customer experience, our second- and third-party partner integrations, and the recommendation and personalization capabilities that shape what consumers see. Scope will flex over time with business priorities, so we're looking for a leader who can operate well across product areas rather than in a single lane.

AI is a core part of this role on both sides of the equation: what we build and how we build it. You'll drive AI into the platforms and customer experiences your teams own — personalization, recommendations, assisted and conversational journeys — and you'll be one of the leaders shaping how our engineers work with AI day to day. Both come with accountability for adoption, quality, and measurable results.

You'll lead through engineering managers and senior engineers, set technical direction, and stay close enough to the details to make good calls under ambiguity.

What You'll Do

Engineering Leadership & Delivery

Lead a multi-team engineering organization; own the roadmap, guide architecture, and delivery across your portfolio of consumer-facing products and platforms.
Set technical direction and engineering standards — architecture, code quality, testing, observability, and operational excellence — and raise the bar on craft and velocity.
Balance feature delivery against platform, tech debt, and reliability investment; make and defend those trade-offs with executive stakeholders.
Define and track the technical and experience metrics (uptime, latency, integration health, conversion, NPS/CSAT) that measure success for your portfolio.

AI in Our Products & Platforms

Own the engineering strategy for embedding AI into the customer experiences your teams build — personalization, recommendations, assisted and conversational journeys, and intelligent automation across the consumer lifecycle.
Build the platform capabilities that make AI features viable at scale: model and LLM integration, retrieval and context pipelines, evaluation harnesses, guardrails, observability, and cost controls.
Partner with Product and Data Science to move AI capabilities from experiment to production — defining success metrics, evaluation criteria, and the path to full rollout.
Apply AI to make our partner integrations and internal platforms smarter — document and data extraction, decisioning support, and operational automation.
Own the responsible-AI posture for what your teams ship: accuracy, explainability, bias, consumer disclosure, and data handling, working with Compliance and Legal.

Product & Customer Experience

Own the logged-in customer experience: the account dashboard, offer and product management, and the ongoing engagement that keeps consumers coming back.
Drive the strategy and execution behind integrations with second- and third-party partners (lenders, servicers, data providers), ensuring they're secure, resilient, and easy to extend as the partner network grows.
Own the product recommendation experience end to end — how offers and next-best actions are surfaced, tested, and refined so each consumer sees the right thing at the right moment.
Partner with Product, Design, and Analytics to translate consumer insight into a roadmap that improves conversion, engagement, retention, and satisfaction across the full customer journey.

People & Partnership

Hire, coach, and develop engineering managers and senior engineers; own performance management, career growth, and org design across your teams.
Represent engineering in cross-functional planning, budgeting, and prioritization, and communicate progress and risk clearly to senior leadership.
Partner with Security, Compliance, and Legal to ensure systems and consumer data handling meet regulatory requirements in financial services.

What You'll Need

10+ years of software engineering experience, including 5+ years in engineering leadership managing managers or multiple teams.
Proven experience owning consumer-facing product areas end to end, with accountability for both delivery and technical health.

jobs.description:
About LeafLink

LeafLink is the largest unified B2B cannabis platform, providing licensed cannabis businesses a suite of tools to manage their business more effectively, sell or order from their favorite brands and accelerate growth. We are one platform, one solution and we’re defining the way thousands of cannabis brands, distributors, and retailers streamline their operations. With thousands of brands and retailers across 30+ markets in North America, we are setting the industry standard for how cannabis businesses grow together. LeafLink processes more than $5 billion in wholesale cannabis orders annually.

Our team, backed by funding from leading VC's, including Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, Nosara Capital, and Lerer Hippeau is poised to define the cannabis supply chain through technology. LeafLink was named one of Inc. 5000’s ‘Top 5000 Fastest-Growing Private Companies’; one of Fast Company's 'Top 10 Most Innovative Companies in Enterprise for 2020', joining the ranks of Amazon, Slack, and VMWare; one of Built In NYC's 'Best Places to Work in 2021'; 2024 Fast Company’s Best WorkPlaces for Innovators for Banking, Finance, and Fintech category; 2024 Green Market Report Award for Best Fintech in cannabis - and we're just getting started!

The Role

LeafLink is seeking a Head of Engineering to lead our entire engineering organization. This role owns the technical vision, architecture, and health of every engineering function and is accountable for how well our teams turn strategy into shipped, reliable software. You'll report directly into executive leadership, partner closely with Product, and represent engineering at the leadership table.

As Head of Engineering, you are the senior-most technical leader responsible for building the org itself: hiring and developing engineering managers, setting standards for how we plan and execute, and making the calls on architecture, tooling, and headcount that determine whether we can keep moving fast without breaking things. You'll work with modern technologies and concepts such as containerized and serverless design patterns, Python, Kubernetes, AWS-managed and self-hosted services, third-party integrations, and event-driven and distributed architectures. This is a rare opportunity to shape not just a roadmap, but the operating model of an engineering org at a pivotal size, big enough to need real structure, small enough that one leader can still touch everything that matters.

Ideal candidates possess a strategic mind for solving unique challenges with fitting solutions, and a track record of building high-performing teams and the managers who run them. They should be personable, decisive, flexible, and communicative, with a strong desire to implement change, grow the org thoughtfully, and bring a genuine passion for their craft. This role comes with the opportunity to define engineering leadership at a fast-paced, dynamic, and quickly growing company.

What You'll Be Doing

Translate company, product, and technology objectives and goals into a 1 - 3-year engineering plan, operating model, organizational structure, and execution roadmap. Lead rebuild versus refactor decisions related to platform enhancement and integration across all of our platforms
Create the right engineering organizational structure and lead the engineering team. Recruit, develop, and retain top engineering talent and set the bar for how the engineering team operates day to day
Set engineering-wide standards for planning, estimation, and delivery, and hold teams accountable to them without turning process into bureaucracy
Establish engineering metrics, operating rhythms, and governance that provide executive visibility into execution. Own and manage the technical architecture, infrastructure, security and technical debt speed and long-term stability.
Improve engineering velocity while reducing technical debt and operational risk.
Partner with product and business stakeholders to translate customer requirements into engineering priorities, ensuring engineering capacity, sequencing, and constraints are represented in roadmap decisions and the team delivers features that have measurable customer impact and move adoption., ensuring
Manage the engineering budget: headcount planning, vendor and tooling spend, and cloud cost, with a clear view of TCO
Establish company-wide engineering practices for code quality, testing, CI/CD, and on-call/incident response as the team scales past the size where informal norms hold
Own SOC 2 and broader security/compliance posture across engineering, partnering with IT and any external auditors
Create long-term sustainable mechanisms such as feedback loops, retros, postmortems, and eng-wide metrics for continuous improvement across performance, scale, delivery and org health.
Build and protect engineering culture as headcount grows: the norms around ownership, blameless problem-solving, and technical excellence that are easy to lose past 80 people
Champion agentic AI, LLM-powered code generation, and multi-agent orchestration to reimagine how services are built and operated at scale, compressing delivery timelines and raising engineering velocity.

What You'll Bring To The Team

12+ years of experience in software engineering, with 7+ years leading engineering managers (not just ICs)
Experience in working in marketplaces or enterprise platforms and building and developing large-scale infrastructure or distributed systems. Experience in e-commerce, B2B SaaS, or marketplace businesses (and their mobile counterparts) a plus
Direct experience building an engineering org from the ground up or through a major scaling inflection point, you've made the "when do we add a second team" calls before
Strong track record setting technical vision and translating it into a roadmap that executive leadership and the board actually trust
Strong balance of technical depth, strategic thinking, and operational leadership. Extensive experience communicating engineering strategy, risk, and resourcing to non-technical executives and board members
Proven experience building and scaling engineering organizations in high-growth or mission-critical environments balancing execution versus management
Hands-on background (even if not day-to-day anymore) with modern cloud-native architecture: AWS-managed services (EKS, ECR, R53, SES, ElastiCache, RDS, etc.), infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible), and containers (Docker, Kubernetes)
Experience owning security and compliance programs, including SOC 2 controls and audit management
Strong experience with CI/CD tooling and practices (Jenkins, CircleCI, ArgoCD, Spinnaker, or similar) and a point of view on developer experience
Experience with API management and service-oriented, API-driven architectures, and the operational challenges they create at scale
Proven ability to manage budget, vendor relationships, and cost efficiency for an engineering org
A genuine passion for developing people, you measure your success by the managers and engineers who grow under you

LeafLink Perks & Benefits

Flexible PTO - you’re going to be working hard so enjoy time off with no cap!
A robust stock option plan to give our employees a direct stake in LeafLink’s success
5 Days of Volunteer Time Off (VTO) - giving back is important to us and we want our employees to prioritize cultivating a better community
Competitive compensation and 401k
Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental, vision)
Commuter Benefits through our Flexible Spending Account

Be one of the Bedo 100

Albedo is making Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) mainstream, building the infrastructure to usher every satellite mission set into this new orbital domain. We build buses, integrated satellites, and turnkey missions for customers to thrive in VLEO, between 250 km - 400 km, where proximity compounds performance and drag self-cleans debris.

As part of the first 100 employees at Albedo, you will have a big impact on Albedo’s trajectory to proliferating VLEO — whether you’re advancing hardware to increase satellite longevity, scaling production for large constellations, building next-gen flight and ground software to push performance, or enabling missions that matter for national security and our day-to-day life here on earth.

How We Operate:
Albedo takes a first-principles approach — in space and in business. We move with speed, take calculated risks, and learn quickly. We use AI regularly to create leverage in every discipline across the company. We work in-person at our Broomfield CO HQ to maximize team and company productivity. We work hard and with urgency to compound our first-mover advantage.

Who We're Looking For:
Builders who want to own outcomes, not tasks. Systems thinkers who balance precision with iteration while thinking about the big picture. Individuals who are energized by creating a category rather than competing in an existing one. You’ll join a team that has already proven what others said wasn’t feasible and is now scaling and upgrading our VLEO buses & payloads to serve mission sets across sensing, communications, and responsive operations.

If you can feel the excitement running through your veins, apply to be one of the Bedo 100.

About This Role

Albedo is building software for satellites that fly in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO). As Director of Software Engineering, you'll lead the teams developing our flight software, GNC, ground systems, and applied AI, and ensure our missions meet their autonomy and performance objectives. This role will ensure long-term growth and adaptation as the pace of software and autonomy accelerates for VLEO and beyond.

What You’ll Do

Lead the software engineering organization — FSW, GNC, applied AI, ground — across approximately three to four teams of managers and ICs
Own the integrated software performance of the satellite: deterministic flight software, control law implementation and verification, on-orbit and on-ground AI, and the command-and-control path
Manage the simulation and HIL infrastructure that scales across the program and stays honestly flight-like
Lead the closure of the GNC analytical-to-flight loop so that anomalies trace cleanly to model gaps or implementation bugs without ambiguity
Develop technical leaders in each software domain (including domains outside your strongest) and resist the gravity to over-invest in your home discipline
Defend the boundary between flight software and ground tooling, and the boundary between software and hardware, against drift
Partner with the Director of Hardware, Systems Engineering, and Program Management to make software a peer of hardware in the system

Your Ideal Skills And Experience

Twelve-plus years in real-time embedded, GNC, or flight software, with at least four leading software engineering managers
Deep fluency in deterministic flight or flight-like software: timing, scheduling, fault containment, C++ on RTOS
GNC literacy at the leadership level - you cannot derive every Kalman variant from scratch, but you can engage substantively with control law structure, estimator behavior, actuator interaction, and their failure modes, and you have done so in your own career
Track record of building simulation and HIL infrastructure that caught real bugs before flight, and post-mortem discipline that changed the pipeline when bugs survived
Experience leading heterogeneous software teams across domains you did not personally come up through
Real opinions on the HW/SW boundary, on-orbit vs ground compute split, and where abstractions earn their keep

Salary Range

$234,323 - $269,600 per year

Compensation And Benefits For Full-Time Roles

Employee friendly equity compensation
4% direct matching 401k
Health Insurance: 100% employee coverage & 75% dependent coverage
Parental leave and childcare coverage
Flexible vacation and sick time from day one
12 company holidays
$100 monthly wellness benefit
Relocation package if not based in Denver

All persons hired will be required to be a U.S. citizen, a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Director of Engineering, Core Database

Yugabyte is seeking an experienced and accomplished Director of Engineering
to lead key aspects of our distributed SQL database development. This leader will drive the architecture, development, and delivery of core transactional, storage, and distributed systems components, ensuring YugabyteDB maintains industry-leading performance, scalability, and resilience. This role requires a mix of software architecture expertise to design and implement practical solutions, as well as the ability to work closely with developers to identify patterns and tools that simplify solution building. You will lead one or more critical engineering teams focused on the heart of YugabyteDB, bringing technical depth in database internals and distributed systems to mentor and grow a world-class engineering organization.

This position demands a blend of hands-on architectural expertise, large-scale systems design,
and the ability to execute against an ambitious product roadmap, with a deep understanding of transactional databases, distributed systems, and microservice-based applications.

Role And Responsibilities

Technical Strategy & Architecture: Define and drive the technical roadmap and architecture for core database components, including the storage engine (LSM/RocksDB), transactional layer, distributed consensus (RAFT), and multi-master replication (xCluster).
Engineering Execution: Own the end-to-end development, quality, performance, and operational excellence of your teams' components, ensuring deployment in cloud-native environments (e.g., Kubernetes).
Team Leadership & Mentorship: Recruit, mentor, and manage high-performing engineering teams. Foster a culture of deep technical ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Systems Scaling & Reliability: Lead projects focused on write scaling, improving concurrency (e.g., DDL concurrency), ensuring cache coherency, and achieving 99.995% availability in distributed, multi-tenant, cloud-native environments.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Product Management, Technical Leadership (TDs/CTO), and other engineering teams (Query Optimizer, QA) to define requirements and deliver integrated, impactful features.

Required Experience

The ideal candidate will have demonstrated senior leadership in domains directly applicable to distributed databases:

Experience: 10+ years of progressive software development experience, with at least 3+ years in a Director role managing multiple teams or critical product areas.
Database Internals Expertise: Substantial experience designing and developing core components of production-grade relational or distributed database engines (e.g., storage/access layer, buffer cache, logging, recovery, lock management, indexing, LSM).
Distributed Systems & Cloud-Native Architectures: Proven ability to design and deliver internet-scale, highly available, multi-tenant distributed systems, leveraging technologies such as Service Fabric, distributed lock managers, distributed transaction managers, and cloud object storage.
Core Programming Languages: Hands-on experience in systems programming languages, particularly C/C++ and Go.
Scalability and Performance: Direct experience resolving performance bottlenecks (e.g., range scans, nested loop joins) and re-architecting systems for massive scaling (e.g., separating log/data, multi-writer architectures).

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

YugabyteDB/PostgreSQL: Experience with PostgreSQL internals or PostgreSQL-compatible distributed databases.
Cloud & Kubernetes: Hands-on experience with modern public cloud infrastructure and cloud-native technologies such as Kubernetes and Prometheus.
NoSQL Databases: Familiarity with NoSQL databases.
Open Source & Research: Contributions to open-source database projects, patents, or successfully integrating research concepts (e.g., ML-based anomaly detection) into products.
Data Technologies: Experience with technologies common in the Yugabyte ecosystem, such as Apache Bookkeeper, Spark, Kafka, or other NoSQL/Graph databases (e.g., Neo4J).

We work in a hybrid model, with the team together in our Sunnyvale office 2–3 days per week.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager (Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access.
We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About Engineering At Headway

Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!).

Principles That Guide Us

Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapist to better solve the problems they're facing.
Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration
Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.
Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

About This Role

You'll lead the Infrastructure team — one of three teams in Engineering Foundations, alongside Agentic Engineering and Eddy, Headway's internal AI platform — that every other team at Headway builds on. You'll own cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, LLM infrastructure (gateway, multi-provider failover, per-team rate limiting), the database platform, observability, and incident response, while hiring and growing a high-performance team shipping at AI-accelerated velocity.

As AI dramatically increases code velocity across the org, our mandate is to make every change safe from the start and build systems that get safer as they get faster, working toward a model where routine infrastructure is self-serve and the team spends the majority of its time on strategic platform work. That means owning the reliability, performance, and scalability of Mamba, Headway's FastAPI/Python monolith, and the AWS infrastructure it runs on. This is a technical leadership role: you'll set strategy and vision for the team, report to the Head of Engineering Foundations, and lead through credibility in design reviews and incident response, not through distance from the work.

What You'll Own

An engineering team: hiring to a high bar into a growing team, developing engineers through the senior and staff levels, and running an effective on-call rotation for a team the rest of engineering depends on.
The infrastructure platform: a system every other Headway team builds on, and a roadmap spanning cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, LLM infrastructure, the data layer, and observability.
The shift from reactive to strategic: driving the team's operating model toward self-serve infrastructure, so the team spends more time on strategic platform work and less on routine support requests.
Blast-radius reduction: leading the architectural and deployment validation work that contains the scope and duration of incidents when they happen.
The org interface: defining production readiness expectations for AI workloads, co-owning container security and secrets management with the Security team, and making sure the platform is accessible and well-understood by the product engineering teams that depend on it.

Who You Are

We're looking for experienced engineering team leaders and people managers who are relationship-obsessed, drive results, and enable their teams to build for technical excellence. As a Senior Engineering Manager at Headway, you will work closely with Engineering Leadership, Security, and product engineering teams across the org to help shape the future of the engineering organization.

You are an infrastructure leader who is as comfortable in a postmortem as you are in a planning doc. You know how to run a team that carries a support queue while still making progress on strategic platform work. You hold the technical bar yourself and earn credibility with the team through the quality of your judgment, not your title.

Experience We're Seeking

5-7+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager, with experience leading infrastructure or platform teams.
5+ years of experience as a Software or Infrastructure Engineer, with enough depth to lead credibly in design reviews and incident response
Experience managing the interface between a platform team and the product engineering teams that depend on it, including setting ownership boundaries and building self-serve tooling
Comfortable managing through competing demands: a support queue, a strategic roadmap, an on-call rotation, and fast-moving external dependencies all at once
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure at scale (AWS), observability tooling (Datadog or similar), and deployment pipelines at companies where reliability is a product requirement
Experience owning a platform strategy and representing it to senior leadership: setting measurable goals for infrastructure work, and making the case for foundational investment in terms the business understands

Below are additional experiences we think help engineering managers succeed at Headway:

You have led a team through a significant architectural transition, such as moving from a monolith toward service isolation, or from manual to automated operations
You have experience building or governing LLM infrastructure and AI platform primitives
You have experience in healthcare or another regulated environment

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Agent Context
jobs.description:
We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the Agent Context team in NYC. This team owns how Asana's AI systems search, retrieve, and reason over the work graph the search infrastructure, dense embedding pipelines, ranking systems, and evaluation frameworks that determine whether every AI experience at Asana is trustworthy or not. Your mission is to make retrieval comprehensive, reliable, and fast at enterprise scale, positioning Asana as the coordination and memory layer for the agentic enterprise.

This is a high-leverage platform role: nearly every AI product at Asana - AI Teammates, chat experiences, agentic workflows depends on the systems this team builds. You will manage a team of senior engineers in New York collaborating daily with partner teams in San Francisco and Warsaw, and work alongside a dedicated Product Manager as your direct counterpart. This role is based in our New York office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday; most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays.

What you'll achieve

Own the technical direction and delivery of Asana's retrieval stack end to end: lexical and semantic search, dense embedding generation and backfill at scale, chunking and ranking strategies, and RAG comprehensiveness across the work graph.
Build and operate the evaluation infrastructure that makes retrieval quality measurable recall/precision benchmarks, offline and online evals, and comparative testing across retrieval backends - so quality decisions are made with data, not vibes.
Drive the cost, performance, and quality tradeoffs that define this space: when semantic search earns its infrastructure cost over lexical, how to hit latency targets without sacrificing recall, and how retrieval improvements compound into cheaper, faster downstream LLM calls.
Set and enforce the bar for how other teams at Asana integrate with retrieval: clear ownership of embedding decisions, rollout guidance, metrics to watch, and a platform posture that says no to unjustified infrastructure spend.
Hire, grow, and retain a team of strong senior engineers in NYC, and lead effectively across three time zones with deliberate async communication practices.
Partner with your PM counterpart to translate a multi-year platform thesis into a sequenced roadmap, and represent the team's technical strategy to engineering and product leadership.

About You

8+ years of software engineering experience with 3+ years managing engineers, including senior engineers, on infrastructure or ML systems teams. You've hired, coached, grown, and when necessary exited engineers and your former reports would work for you again.
You have shipped and operated production search, retrieval, or ML-serving systems at meaningful scale. You can speak concretely about systems you've run: the index architecture, the embedding models, the latency budgets, the incidents, and what you'd do differently.
Deep working knowledge of the modern retrieval stack inverted indexes and BM25, vector search and embedding models, hybrid retrieval, chunking strategies, re-ranking and strong opinions about when each is worth its cost. You should be able to argue both sides of "semantic search everywhere" and tell us where you actually land.
You've built or heavily used evaluation systems for ML/AI quality: golden datasets, recall/precision metrics, LLM-as-judge, online experimentation. You believe unmeasured quality claims are noise.
You're technically credible enough to review a design doc for an embedding backfill or an OpenSearch mapping change and catch the problem the team missed. You don't need to write the code, but engineers should leave design reviews with you sharper than they arrived.
You've led distributed teams across time zones and know that it runs on written communication. You write clearly, decisively, and often.
Experience with LLM-powered products, agent systems, or RAG pipelines in production is strongly preferred. Experience scaling a platform team that serves internal customers is a plus.

What we'll offer

Our comprehensive compensation package plays a big part in how we recognize you for the impact you have on our path to achieving our mission. We believe that compensation should be reflective of the value you create relative to the market value of your role. To ensure pay is fair and not impacted by biases, we're committed to looking at market value which is why we check ourselves and conduct a yearly pay equity audit.

. The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. The listed range above is a guideline, and the base salary range for this role may be modified.

Asana is a leading platform for human + AI collaboration. Millions of teams around the world rely on Asana to achieve their most important goals, faster. jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager (Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access.
We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About Engineering At Headway

Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!).

Principles That Guide Us

Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapist to better solve the problems they're facing.
Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration
Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.
Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

About This Role

You'll lead the Infrastructure team — one of three teams in Engineering Foundations, alongside Agentic Engineering and Eddy, Headway's internal AI platform — that every other team at Headway builds on. You'll own cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, LLM infrastructure (gateway, multi-provider failover, per-team rate limiting), the database platform, observability, and incident response, while hiring and growing a high-performance team shipping at AI-accelerated velocity.

As AI dramatically increases code velocity across the org, our mandate is to make every change safe from the start and build systems that get safer as they get faster, working toward a model where routine infrastructure is self-serve and the team spends the majority of its time on strategic platform work. That means owning the reliability, performance, and scalability of Mamba, Headway's FastAPI/Python monolith, and the AWS infrastructure it runs on. This is a technical leadership role: you'll set strategy and vision for the team, report to the Head of Engineering Foundations, and lead through credibility in design reviews and incident response, not through distance from the work.

What You'll Own

An engineering team: hiring to a high bar into a growing team, developing engineers through the senior and staff levels, and running an effective on-call rotation for a team the rest of engineering depends on.
The infrastructure platform: a system every other Headway team builds on, and a roadmap spanning cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, LLM infrastructure, the data layer, and observability.
The shift from reactive to strategic: driving the team's operating model toward self-serve infrastructure, so the team spends more time on strategic platform work and less on routine support requests.
Blast-radius reduction: leading the architectural and deployment validation work that contains the scope and duration of incidents when they happen.
The org interface: defining production readiness expectations for AI workloads, co-owning container security and secrets management with the Security team, and making sure the platform is accessible and well-understood by the product engineering teams that depend on it.

Who You Are

We're looking for experienced engineering team leaders and people managers who are relationship-obsessed, drive results, and enable their teams to build for technical excellence. As a Senior Engineering Manager at Headway, you will work closely with Engineering Leadership, Security, and product engineering teams across the org to help shape the future of the engineering organization.

You are an infrastructure leader who is as comfortable in a postmortem as you are in a planning doc. You know how to run a team that carries a support queue while still making progress on strategic platform work. You hold the technical bar yourself and earn credibility with the team through the quality of your judgment, not your title.

Experience We're Seeking

5-7+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager, with experience leading infrastructure or platform teams.
5+ years of experience as a Software or Infrastructure Engineer, with enough depth to lead credibly in design reviews and incident response
Experience managing the interface between a platform team and the product engineering teams that depend on it, including setting ownership boundaries and building self-serve tooling
Comfortable managing through competing demands: a support queue, a strategic roadmap, an on-call rotation, and fast-moving external dependencies all at once
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure at scale (AWS), observability tooling (Datadog or similar), and deployment pipelines at companies where reliability is a product requirement
Experience owning a platform strategy and representing it to senior leadership: setting measurable goals for infrastructure work, and making the case for foundational investment in terms the business understands

Below are additional experiences we think help engineering managers succeed at Headway:

You have led a team through a significant architectural transition, such as moving from a monolith toward service isolation, or from manual to automated operations
You have experience building or governing LLM infrastructure and AI platform primitives
You have experience in healthcare or another regulated environment

If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please inform the recruiter when they contact you to schedule your interview.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager (Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access.
We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About Engineering At Headway

Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!).

Principles That Guide Us

Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapist to better solve the problems they're facing.
Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration
Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.
Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

About This Role

You'll lead the Infrastructure team — one of three teams in Engineering Foundations, alongside Agentic Engineering and Eddy, Headway's internal AI platform — that every other team at Headway builds on. You'll own cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, LLM infrastructure (gateway, multi-provider failover, per-team rate limiting), the database platform, observability, and incident response, while hiring and growing a high-performance team shipping at AI-accelerated velocity.

As AI dramatically increases code velocity across the org, our mandate is to make every change safe from the start and build systems that get safer as they get faster, working toward a model where routine infrastructure is self-serve and the team spends the majority of its time on strategic platform work. That means owning the reliability, performance, and scalability of Mamba, Headway's FastAPI/Python monolith, and the AWS infrastructure it runs on. This is a technical leadership role: you'll set strategy and vision for the team, report to the Head of Engineering Foundations, and lead through credibility in design reviews and incident response, not through distance from the work.

What You'll Own

An engineering team: hiring to a high bar into a growing team, developing engineers through the senior and staff levels, and running an effective on-call rotation for a team the rest of engineering depends on.
The infrastructure platform: a system every other Headway team builds on, and a roadmap spanning cloud infrastructure, deployment pipelines, LLM infrastructure, the data layer, and observability.
The shift from reactive to strategic: driving the team's operating model toward self-serve infrastructure, so the team spends more time on strategic platform work and less on routine support requests.
Blast-radius reduction: leading the architectural and deployment validation work that contains the scope and duration of incidents when they happen.
The org interface: defining production readiness expectations for AI workloads, co-owning container security and secrets management with the Security team, and making sure the platform is accessible and well-understood by the product engineering teams that depend on it.

Who You Are

We're looking for experienced engineering team leaders and people managers who are relationship-obsessed, drive results, and enable their teams to build for technical excellence. As a Senior Engineering Manager at Headway, you will work closely with Engineering Leadership, Security, and product engineering teams across the org to help shape the future of the engineering organization.

You are an infrastructure leader who is as comfortable in a postmortem as you are in a planning doc. You know how to run a team that carries a support queue while still making progress on strategic platform work. You hold the technical bar yourself and earn credibility with the team through the quality of your judgment, not your title.

Experience We're Seeking

5-7+ years of experience as an Engineering Manager, with experience leading infrastructure or platform teams.
5+ years of experience as a Software or Infrastructure Engineer, with enough depth to lead credibly in design reviews and incident response
Experience managing the interface between a platform team and the product engineering teams that depend on it, including setting ownership boundaries and building self-serve tooling
Comfortable managing through competing demands: a support queue, a strategic roadmap, an on-call rotation, and fast-moving external dependencies all at once
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure at scale (AWS), observability tooling (Datadog or similar), and deployment pipelines at companies where reliability is a product requirement
Experience owning a platform strategy and representing it to senior leadership: setting measurable goals for infrastructure work, and making the case for foundational investment in terms the business understands

Below are additional experiences we think help engineering managers succeed at Headway:

You have led a team through a significant architectural transition, such as moving from a monolith toward service isolation, or from manual to automated operations
You have experience building or governing LLM infrastructure and AI platform primitives
You have experience in healthcare or another regulated environment

If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please inform the recruiter when they contact you to schedule your interview.

Cambium is the AI-powered platform modernizing the wood economy, and we're looking for a seasoned engineering leader whose business instincts are as sharp as their technical depth. This is as much about building well on existing platforms (Netsuite, Hubspot, etc.) as it is greenfield.
